title: How can I make better use of AI for the graphics in my indie game?
author: Pale-Candidate-4122
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I'm a hobbyist programmer working on a 2D action game called **Avoid Bubbles Game**, made with C++ and raylib.

Programming is my main interest, but I'm honestly not very good at creating graphics or artwork. So far, I've been using AI-generated assets in my project, but I feel that the visual style could be much more consistent and polished.

I'm not looking to have AI make the entire game for me. I want to use it as a tool to help with the parts I'm less skilled at, especially art and visual design.

I'd love to hear your advice:

* Which AI tools would you recommend for creating consistent 2D game assets?
* How can I maintain a coherent art style across characters, enemies, backgrounds, and UI?
* Are there any good workflows for generating and refining game assets with AI?
* How do you handle animations and keeping characters visually consistent across multiple frames?

Here's my current project if you'd like to take a look:

**Free browser demo:** [https://kc-games-studio.itch.io/avoid-b](https://kc-games-studio.itch.io/avoid-b)

Any recommendations, tools, or personal experiences would be greatly appreciated. Thanks!

comments.author: egod
comments.body: Your step1 will be to make your own 2D studio animation with AI. From there, you will set up your arts style guide line and animation fluidity. Then the AI will use it directly and make stuff for you on demand.
